technical-director.d: Technical directors realise the artistic visions of the creators within technical constraints. They coordinate the operations of various production units, such as scene, wardrobe, sound and lighting, and make-up. They adapt the prototype and study the feasibility, implementation, operation and technical monitoring of…

n.story:
Your role is shifting from a logistical coordinator to a high-level creative technologist. While you once spent hours drafting risk assessments and manually syncing rehearsal schedules, AI now generates these documents in seconds based on your technical specs. This shift liberates you to focus on the 'impossible' creative demands of artists. Instead of saying 'no' due to technical constraints, you use generative simulation tools to prototype complex stage effects and lighting environments instantly, showing designers exactly how their vision will translate to a specific venue's physical footprint.

In the heat of production, your value lies in human-centric leadership. While AI monitors the technical health of the rig and suggests safety optimizations, you are the one negotiating with temperamental talent and managing the interpersonal dynamics of a diverse technical crew. You become the bridge between digital precision and the unpredictable, visceral nature of live performance, using data-driven insights to ensure that every creative risk is backed by a robust, AI-verified safety net.
auto: Scheduling rehearsal blocks and room bookings
Initial venue acoustic and lighting mapping
Basic budget tracking and resource logging
amp: Rapid prototyping of complex creative stage demands
Real-time safety monitoring via computer vision
Advanced spatial simulation for venue adaptation
Data-backed negotiation for technical resources
Predictive maintenance for stage machinery
tools: AI-powered project management and scheduling platforms
n.adv: Focus on mastering generative design and spatial simulation tools; your future value lies in your ability to rapidly translate an artist's abstract vision into a technically viable, AI-simulated reality.

metal-drawing-machine-operator.d: Metal drawing machine operators set up and operate drawing machines for ferrous and non-ferrous metal products, designed to provide wires, bars, pipes, hollow profiles and tubes with their specific form by reducing its cross-section and by pulling the working materials through a series of drawing dies.

n.story:
The days of standing by a machine to monitor gauges and manually pull defective workpieces are fading. Your role is evolving into that of a 'Process Optimizer.' AI systems now handle the constant vigilance required for quality control, using high-speed sensors to detect microscopic flaws that the human eye would miss. This transition removes you from the repetitive, physically taxing aspects of the shop floor and moves you into a control-room environment where you oversee a fleet of automated drawing lines.

You now spend your time troubleshooting complex system anomalies that the AI flags but cannot solve. You use predictive analytics to adjust cycle times and material throughput, optimizing for both speed and die longevity. Your deep knowledge of metal properties remains essential, but it is now applied through a digital twin of the factory. You are no longer just an operator; you are a technical specialist who fine-tunes the intelligence of the machines to achieve near-zero defect rates.
auto: Routine data logging and cycle timing
amp: Predictive maintenance and anomaly detection
Multi-variable process optimization
Advanced troubleshooting of automated systems

While your physical dexterity is still vital for bespoke assembly and complex joins, AI and robotics are taking over the most monotonous tasks like fastening components and basic quality checks. You will find yourself working alongside 'cobots' (collaborative robots) that handle the heavy lifting and repetitive motions, while you act as the expert technician who ensures everything meets exacting standards.

Your ability to troubleshoot will be significantly amplified by AI diagnostic tools that can parse technical documentation in seconds to find solutions for rare assembly errors. You will transition from 'doing' to 'verifying,' using computer vision systems to catch microscopic defects that were previously invisible. This evolution turns you into a high-tech craftsman, where your deep knowledge of metal properties is supported by real-time data, making the assembly process safer, faster, and much more accurate.

data-entry-supervisor.d: Data entry supervisors manage the day-to-day operations of data entry staff. They organise the workflow and tasks.

n.story:
Your role is undergoing a radical shift from managing people who type to managing the algorithms that ingest. As OCR and LLMs reach near-perfect proficiency in data extraction, the manual 'entry' part of your department's name effectively disappears. You will no longer spend your days auditing keystrokes or resolving manual typos; instead, you will act as a 'Data Orchestrator,' using natural language to generate complex queries in MDX, SQL, or SPARQL that once required specialized coding knowledge. 

This automation of technical syntax frees you to focus on the human and strategic elements of your role. You will transition from a technical bottleneck to a high-level supervisor of data integrity and team morale. Your week will shift toward synthesizing AI-generated feedback into actionable insights for your department and focusing on the 'soft' side of leadership—motivating your team as their roles also evolve and ensuring that the data being processed aligns with complex company policies and ethical standards.

hearse-driver.d: Hearse drivers operate and maintain specialised vehicles to transport deceased persons from their homes, hospital or funeral home to their final resting place. They also assist the funeral attendants with their duties.

n.story:
Your role remains fundamentally stable because it is rooted in physical presence and the solemnity of the occasion, though the 'driving' aspect is becoming increasingly high-tech. While autonomous systems will take over the technical precision of parking, maintaining steady speeds in funeral processions, and navigating traffic laws, the human element of your job—maintaining the vehicle's pristine appearance and the physical handling of heavy weights—remains a manual necessity. 

AI acts as a silent co-pilot, enhancing safety through advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS) that interpret traffic signals and road conditions more accurately than the human eye. This allows you to focus more on the logistical coordination and the dignified execution of the ceremony. You aren't being replaced by a robot; rather, your vehicle is becoming a smart environment that handles the stress of navigation so you can maintain the professional decorum required by the families you serve.

You are no longer just solving heat transfer problems; you are orchestrating complex energy ecosystems. Your value lies in your engineering judgment—validating AI-generated models for safety, navigating novel physical constraints that data hasn't yet captured, and leading the transition to next-generation geothermal and electric heating solutions.

enterprise-development-worker.d: Enterprise development workers support enterprises in solving big social problems by liaising with communities and customers. They strive to improve the productivity of employees and the health of their families by focusing on the work-life balance.

You use AI-powered predictive modeling to identify which aircraft or operators are at the highest risk of a future incident, allowing for proactive rather than reactive inspections. Your interpersonal skills become even more vital as you liaise with management to enforce safety cultures, using AI-generated evidence to back your high-stakes decisions. You remain the ultimate authority on airworthiness, but your decisions are now powered by comprehensive, real-time global safety data.
